author: Augustine

passages.original: sed nec uos ipsos, quod ab imperatore basilicae uobis ut redderentur petistis, arguimus, tamquam in Iuliano principe speraueritis, sed arguimus, quod de Christi testimonio desperaueritis, a cuius unitate ipsas basilicas separastis. eas enim iubente inimico Christi accepistis, in quibus iussa Christi contemneretis, dum ualidum et uerum uobis uidetur quod Iulianus constituit dicens: hoc quoque supplicantibus Rogatiano, Pontio, Cassiano et ceteris episcopis, sed et clericis, accedit ad cumulum, ut abolitis, quae aduersus eos sine rescripto perperam gesta sunt, in antiquum statum cuncta reuocentur, inualidum autem et falsum quod Christus constituit dicens: eritis mihi testes in Hierusalem et in totam Iudaeam et Samariam et usque in totam terram.
passages.english: But neither do we reproach you yourselves for having petitioned the emperor that the basilicas be restored to you, as though you had put your hope in the emperor Julian; rather, we reproach you because you have despaired of the testimony of Christ, from whose unity you have separated those very basilicas. For at the command of an enemy of Christ you received them, in order that in them you might despise the commands of Christ, since to you what Julian decreed seems valid and true, when he said: "This too, at the petition of Rogatianus, Pontius, Cassianus and the other bishops, and also the clergy, is added to the sum [of our favours]: that, the measures wrongly taken against them without a rescript being annulled, all things be restored to their former state"; but what Christ decreed seems to you invalid and false, when he said: "You shall be my witnesses in Jerusalem and in all Judaea and Samaria and even to the whole earth."
passages.notes: "accedit ad cumulum" is idiomatic ("is added to the heap/total"), here taken as an addition to the benefits granted. The quotation of Christ is Acts 1:8.
